statement: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid of Quraysh was a merchant of standing and wealth who hired men to trade with her goods for a share of the profit.
Hearing of his truthfulness and trustworthiness she offered him her goods to take to Syria with her servant Maysarah.
He returned with good profit and Maysarah told her of his conduct.
notes: Reports of wonders seen by Maysarah on the journey are left out.

statement: Khadijah proposed marriage through her friend Nafisah bint Munyah; he consulted his uncles and the marriage was concluded.
He was twenty-five; her age is most commonly reported as forty, with other reports giving a younger age.
alternatives: Some reports give her age as twenty-eight.

statement: He did not marry another woman until she died.
notes: Content machine-checked in the Sahih Muslim dataset (narrated by Aishah); Abd al-Baqi number from memory.

statement: All his children except Ibrahim were from Khadijah: al-Qasim, Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, Fatimah and Abdullah; the sons died in childhood.
He said of Khadijah: from her I had children.
Zayd ibn Harithah was freed and raised as a son and was called Zayd ibn Muhammad until the verse 'Call them by their fathers' was revealed.
notes: The hadith and verse are machine-checked; that Zayd came into the household as a servant given by Khadijah is from the Seerah.

statement: Ali ibn Abi Talib was raised in his household to ease Abu Talib's burden.
When he was thirty-five Quraysh rebuilt the Ka'bah after it was damaged by a flood.
He carried stones for the Ka'bah; his uncle al-Abbas suggested he put his waist-cloth on his shoulder; he fell to the ground and covered himself, and was never seen uncovered after that.

The clans disputed over placing the Black Stone; they agreed the first man to enter would judge; it was him; they said 'This is the Trustworthy'; he placed the stone on a cloak, the clan leaders lifted it, and he set it in place with his own hands.
notes: Also reported in Musnad Ahmad; reviewer to add the graded reference.

statement: Aishah: she was not jealous of any wife as she was of Khadijah, whom she never saw; he mentioned her often and sent portions of meat to her friends.
Jibril told him to give Khadijah greetings from her Lord and glad tidings of a house in Paradise with no noise and no weariness.
The best of its women was Maryam and the best of its women is Khadijah.
notes: Machine-checked. The Arabic is 'khayru nisa'iha' (the best of its women); 'of her time' follows the common explanation. Reviewer to approve the rendering.

statement: Fifteen years after the marriage, at the first revelation, he returned trembling to Khadijah.
notes: Fifteen years follows from the reported ages of twenty-five and forty.
